label: White shark, tag 118845
title: Satellite tracking data of white sharks in the southwest Indian Ocean (2012-2014)
place: South African coast to southern Mozambique
method: Wildlife Computers SPOT5 satellite transmitter on the dorsal fin; positions by Argos (Doppler) when the fin is at the surface
sample_sentence: 34 sharks were tagged in this study. This is a sample size, not a population estimate.
time_convention: Times are as recorded in the dataset, which the record states are UTC.
location_uncertainty: an Argos quality class per fix; no error figure per fix in the dataset

land_data.source: Natural Earth 1:10m land polygons, github.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector at commit ca96624a56bd078437bca8184e78163e5039ad19 (VERSION 5.2.0-pre)

accuracy_note: Positions are Argos satellite fixes. Each carries a quality class. The satellite system's nominal error estimates are under 250 m (class 3), 250–500 m (2), 500–1,500 m (1) and over 1,500 m (0); classes A and B have no estimate. These are nominal estimates, not guaranteed limits: real errors can be larger.
simplification: filtered, not thinned or smoothed: see the stages. This is not the study's modelled track

rule.speed_limit_source: the study authors' filter parameter (Kock et al. 2022, following Queiroz et al. 2019)

stages.stage: rows for tag 118845 in the source file
speed consistency (experimental rule; limit 3 m/s; classes 3 2 1 first)
more than 72 hours from any other kept fix
on land in the pinned Natural Earth 1:10m land file

gap_rule.statement: Mother Earth does not join fixes more than 12 hours apart, or where the line would cross land in its land map. These are display rules of Mother Earth's, not part of the study.

card.note: Recorded Argos satellite fixes of one white shark, 9 May 2012 to 29 Sep 2013, after filtering. A dated replay, not current. Experimental.
card.shown: 755 recorded fixes of one shark (tag 118845). 69% of them are the two weakest Argos classes, A and B.
card.done: 1,004 recorded fixes for this tag. Mother Earth left out 208 under its own speed-consistency rule (3 m/s, the study authors' limit; the rule favours better-rated fixes, is experimental and can remove a correct fix), 1 more than 72 hours from any other, and 40 that fall on land in Natural Earth's 1:10m map. 755 are shown. Fixes more than 12 hours apart, and 2 pairs whose joining line would cross land in that map, are not joined.
card.line: The line joins recorded fixes no more than 12 hours apart: 616 of 754 steps. It is not the shark's route. For most of the period there is no line.
card.not_route: Recorded Argos fixes after filtering. This is not the study's modelled track, and not a reconstruction of where the shark went.
card.changes: Changes made to the dataset (CC BY 4.0): one tag selected; fixes left out by the stages listed; nothing moved, smoothed or interpolated; the tag number is shown in place of the name in the file.
